newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela and IMF see five pct growth in 1998.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela and IMF see five pct growth in 1998.

text.p: The Venezuelan government and International Monetary Fund see the Venezuelan economy growing between 3.5 and four percent in 1997 and by five percent in 1998, Finance Minister Luis Raul Matos Azocar said Tuesday.
"Growth in 1997 will be lower than in 1998. The IMF says it will be between 3.5 and four percent this year and for 1998 it is estimated at more than five percent," Matos told a news conference.
Matos was speaking after a recent trip to Washington where Venezuelan and IMF officials agreed to extend for another 18 months a one year stand-by economic program that expires in July.
Under the extended program, Venezuela will maintain a tight reign on fiscal accounts with an overall fiscal balance expected in 1997 and 1998, Matos said.
"The global deficit will be zero," he said.
Inflation in 1998 would be lower than this year, he added. "We're talking about between 13.5 percent and 14 percent,", he said.
The government's 1997 inflation target of 30 to 35 percent was recently endorsed by the IMF provided government spending remains in check.
